subject: Request: temporary fairness exception and elevated burst for LaunchLabs Sept rollout
messages:
From: Tom Brewer <tom@launchlabs.ai>
To: aisha_rahman@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 8 Sep 2026 14:05:00 +0000
Subject: Request: temporary elevated throughput for LaunchLabs Sept 15 launch

Hi Aisha,

Quick one — LaunchLabs is going live with a high-visibility feature on Sept 15 and our expected real-time inference traffic for the first 72 hours will exceed our current committed tier. We ran the load forecasts and attached a workbook; peak QPS is expected to be ~4.5x our baseline, coming in short bursts around product events and promos.

Two asks:
- Can Redwood grant a temporary elevated burst allowance / priority lane for the launch window (we're requesting 72 hours, UTC 2026-09-15 00:00 to 2026-09-18 00:00)?
- Can you confirm SLA behavior during that window (latency targets, whether throttling/fairness rules will apply to us)?

We understand platform fairness is important — we’re open to a conditional carveout (monitoring + hard rollback) and will accept any guardrails you need. This launch could materially affect our expansion (we have a paid pilot currently).

I've included Ops (ops@launchlabs.ai) and attached the traffic forecast + a SOC2 snippet you requested earlier.

Thanks — appreciate a quick read and whether we can get a proposal by EOD tomorrow.

Best,
Tom Brewer
Head of Platform, LaunchLabs
attachments: LaunchLabs_traffic_forecast_Q3.xlsx, LaunchLabs_SOC2_snippet.pdf

From: aisha_rahman@redwood.ai <aisha_rahman@redwood.ai>
To: Tom Brewer <tom@launchlabs.ai>
Cc: vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai, grace_oconnor@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 8 Sep 2026 16:18:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Request: temporary elevated throughput for LaunchLabs Sept 15 launch

Tom — thanks for the heads-up and the attachments. We can support escalations like this but need to align on a few specifics so we can scope the operational and risk controls. Quick clarifying questions: 

1) Can you share a short traffic profile (minute-level peaks for the 72-hr window) and worst-case qps? The attached workbook is helpful but we need the per-minute spike table for the SRE team.
2) Are you proposing all traffic to be eligible for priority routing, or just a subset of critical routes (e.g., model inference for the real-time recommendation endpoint only)?
3) Any contractual constraints on latency SLAs during burst windows (e.g., must we guarantee 99th pct latency <= X ms)?

I’ve looped in Vivek (account lead) and Grace (solutions) so we can draft a technical mitigations plan and a commercial proposal (temporary uplift + overage pricing or a short addendum). We'll aim to propose a safe plan by tomorrow EOD — if you can get the minute-level spikes that will speed things up.

--
Aisha Rahman
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
aisha_rahman@redwood.ai
attachments: none

From: grace_oconnor@redwood.ai <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>
To: aisha_rahman@redwood.ai, vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 9 Sep 2026 01:04:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Request: temporary elevated throughput for LaunchLabs Sept 15 launch — proposed mitigations

Folks — reviewed the workbook. Summary and proposed engineering approach: 

Summary:
- Baseline qps: ~1200; projected instantaneous peak: ~5400 (4.5x) with most spikes lasting 30s–3m.
- Traffic is concentrated on /v1/recommend endpoint (85% of requests).

Proposed mitigations (safe default + customer carveout):
1) Temporary priority token pool (tenant-priority lane): allocate a bounded pool equal to 2x baseline throughput for a 48-hour window (instead of 72) to limit risk to platform fairness. Rationale: reduces impact surface and gives LaunchLabs higher success rate for critical requests.

2) Soft-fallback policy: requests over the priority pool will be routed to a compatible quantized model variant with slightly higher latency but lower compute cost. This preserves availability rather than hard-throttling.

3) Auto-threshold rollback: if platform-wide health metrics (region latency P95 or error-rate) degrade > 5% vs baseline for 10+ minutes, priority pool is suspended automatically.

4) Monitoring & runbook: stream real-time token usage + alerts to both parties; provide an SRE runbook (attached) with on-call contacts and rollback steps.

Commercial controls suggestion (for Sales): temporary uplift fee for the 48-hour window + per-token overage tier if we exceed the priority pool. Recommended: 1.5x per-token rate for the burst window.

Notes: this approach balances availability for the customer with platform fairness. If Sales wants to approve 72 hours instead, we should escalate for a higher priority carveout and legal sign-off due to larger systemic risk.

Attachment: redwood_runbook_temp-priority-lane.md

--
Grace O'Connor
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
grace_oconnor@redwood.ai

From: vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>
To: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, aisha_rahman@redwood.ai, grace_oconnor@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 9 Sep 2026 06:12:00 +0000
Subject: Approval request: LaunchLabs temporary priority lane (48h)

Marissa — looping you in to approve the proposed 48-hour temporary priority lane for LaunchLabs (proposal summarized below). We believe it's low risk given the bounded pool + automatic rollback and the commercial uplift. Key points: 
- Window: 2026-09-15 00:00 UTC to 2026-09-17 00:00 UTC (48 hours)
- Priority pool size: 2x baseline (approx 2400 qps sustained burst headroom)
- Soft-fallback to quantized variant for overflow
- Auto-suspend if region P95 latency + error-rate exceed thresholds (runbook attached)
- Commercial: 1.5x token rate for traffic served from priority pool; standard overage beyond that tier.

Estimated revenue protection: enables LaunchLabs paid pilot to scale into a larger account; estimated incremental ARR if successful: $180k-$240k.

Requesting sign-off (technical + commercial) so we can confirm with LaunchLabs today.

Thanks,
Vivek

From: aisha_rahman@redwood.ai <aisha_rahman@redwood.ai>
To: Tom Brewer <tom@launchlabs.ai>
Cc: ops@launchlabs.ai, vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai, grace_oconnor@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 9 Sep 2026 09:22:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Request: temporary elevated throughput for LaunchLabs Sept 15 launch — approved (48h, conditional)

Tom — thanks for the extra detail. We can approve a conditional temporary priority lane for LaunchLabs with the following terms: 

Window: 2026-09-15 00:00 UTC through 2026-09-17 00:00 UTC (48 hours).
Scope: priority routing applied to /v1/recommend only (as requested in your clarified note).
Token pool: bounded pool sized to 2x baseline throughput (see attached runbook for exact values).
Fallback: overflow traffic will be routed to a compatible quantized model variant (preserves availability).
Auto-rollback: priority lane will be suspended automatically if region P95 latency or error-rate degrades > 5% for 10 minutes.
Commercial: 1.5x per-token rate for traffic served from the priority pool during the window; standard overage rules beyond the pool.
Requirements for launch:
- LaunchLabs to provide minute-level spike CSV by EOD today (we need it for SRE telemetry).
- A signed short addendum (DocuSign link below) acknowledging the rollback conditions and temporary rates.

Attachments: redwood_runbook_temp-priority-lane.md (operational runbook), LaunchLabs_traffic_forecast_Q3.xlsx (customer-provided)
DocuSign: https://docusign.com/r/redwood/LL-2026-burst-addendum (draft)
HubSpot deal: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/12345/deal/LL-2026-09-08

Please confirm acceptance of the above and upload the minute-level spikes to the shared folder; we'll flip the switch once DocuSign is countersigned and we've validated telemetry ingestion.

Cheers,
Aisha Rahman
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
aisha_rahman@redwood.ai
attachments: redwood_runbook_temp-priority-lane.md
